newsitem.title: USA: KeyCorp seeks securities firm, no serious talks.
newsitem.headline: KeyCorp seeks securities firm, no serious talks.

text.p: KeyCorp, a bank and financial holding company, said it continues to scout for a securities firm for a possible acquisition, but is not in serious talks at the moment.

"The number of major regional firms is very limited. The pricing is huge. We're not currently seriously talking with anybody," Henry Meyer III, vice chairman and chief operating officer, said after remarks at a Piper Jaffray investors conference here.
KeyCorp already has a brokerage unit, Key Investments Inc (KII).
Meyer added that KeyCorp is looking to increase its fee income, which currently is about 26 percent of total revenues.
"We'd like that number to be higher," Meyer said. "That's really at the low end, and that's why the focus (is on) securities and insurance."
He added KeyCorp is looking to expand as a seller and distributor of insurance, but not as an underwriter.

Meyer said he did not expect KeyCorp to make any further acquisitions in the consumer finance area, following the $200 million purchase of home equity finance company Champion Mortgage and the purchase of Leasetec Corp.
He added that "1998 may see some action, but for the remainder of 1997 we are going to digest Leasetec and Champion Mortgage."
